Md. Abdul Khaleque, AAG ------ For the State.
full_judgment:
Md. Rezaul Haque J: On an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 24-11-2010 passed in Special Tribunal Case No. 18 of 2005, arising out of Nalitabari PS Case No. 14 dated 30-10-2005, corresponding to GR No. 113 of 2005 convicting the petitioner under section 19 A of the Arms Act and sentencing him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 10 years, should not be quashed. 

 2. Facts of the case, in short, are that one Md. Nurul Amin being informant lodged a First Information Report with Nalitabari police station on 30-10-2005 alleging, inter alia, that on 29-10-2005 at about 18-00 hours the informant and his forces got secret information that 4 accused persons were staying with one motor cycle at village kalakuma and on the basis of the said information they went there and they saw one motor cycle and they did not see any man in that place and sat there and thereafter at night at about 21-00 hours they found that one man was coming through middle field by walking, then they caught Badar Uddin alias Zahid and searched his body and recovered country made pipe gun and 6 bullets and other seized it and prepared the seizure-list, hence the case. 

 3. The police of the Nalitabari police station investigated the case and having found prima-facie case submitted a charge-sheet against the accused- petitioner under section 19A of the Arms Act. Ultimately the case record was transmitted to the Special Tribunal No.3, Sherpur and it was registered as Special Tribunal Case No. 18 of 2005. Charge was so framed against the accused person, the petitioner pleaded not guilty of the offence and demanded to be tried as per provisions of law. 

 5. As the petitioner could not prefer appeal within the statutory period of limitation, he has filed this miscellaneous case under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the instant Rule. 

 6. Mr. Md. Habibur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused petitioner has submitted that it is a case of no evidence since the prosecution witnesses did not support the prosecution case. The learned Advocate has further submitted that as per prosecution story one country made pipe gun was recovered but no witness has supported the prosecution story. The learned Advocate has further contended that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove the absolute control and possession of the petitioner over the alleged arms, thus, it is a case of no evidence, accordingly, the judgment and order of conviction and sentence is liable to be quashed. 

 9. It is evident from the record that prosecution examined as many as 11 witnesses out of them PWI JCO Nayek Subeder Md. Nurul Amin is the informant of this case, in his examination in chief stated that the occurrence took place on 29-10-2005 at about 18-00 o'clock. The informant and his forces got secret information as to that 4 accused persons were staying with one motor cycle at village kalakuma and on the basis of said secret information they went there and they saw the motor cycle and they did not see any man in that place and sat there and thereafter at night at about 21.00 hours they found that one man was coming through the middle field by walking, then they caught Babar Uddin alias Zahid and on searching his body got country made one pipe gun and 6 bullets from his body, and then prepared a seizure list in presence of the witnesses. In cross examination, he has categorically stated- 

 19. PW 11 SI Narzyan Chandra Gosh is the Investigation Officer of this case, in his examination in chief he stated that he was appointed as Investigation Officer of this case, during investigation he visited the place of occurrence, prepared sketch map along with index, recorded statements under sections 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and having found prima-facie case submitted charge-sheet against the accused person. In cross examination, he denied the suggestions given by the defence. 

 21. From the above evidence of the witnesses it appears to us that the prosecution claimed that the one country made pipe gun and some cartridges were recovered from the body of one Badurddin but there is nothing against the present convict petitioner, Prosecution witnesses No.1 to 8 have not deposed anything as to recovery of the incriminating articles from the control and possession of the present petitioner. PW 9 is formal witness and PW 10 is the seizure list witness, but PW 10 has not deposed anything against this petitioner. PW II is the investigating officer of this case. So, it is clear that none of the witness has supported the evidence of PW 1, the informant. It also appears to us that though the accused person was apprehended by the police as per evidence of the prosecution witnesses but no arms or ammunitions were recovered from this petitioner. In an arms case the absolute, control and conscious possession of the incriminating article is mandatory for convicting any person, but in the instant case we do not find any such evidence. Thus, we are of the view that it is a case of no evidence, accordingly, the order of conviction and sentence under the said section of the Arms Act cannot be sustained, as such, the judgment and order of conviction and sentence is not maintainable in the eye of law and liable to be quashed. 

 22. In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 24-11-2010 passed in Special Tribunal Case No. 18 of 2005, arising out of Nalitabari PS Case No. 14 dated 30-10-2005, corresponding to GR No. 113 of 2005 is hereby quashed. Let the petitioner Mostafa be set at liberty at once, if not wanted in connection with in any other case.
